name: pdk-dbt-openai-dbt
instr:
Since we moved nightly jobs to the Batch API and put a few projects on flex and priority processing, `openai__cost_usage_report` from the dbt package in /app no longer adds up per project. A project that only runs batch jobs is charged a blended rate. A sample of November's `completion` and `cost` tables is in /data/openai.

The report needs a `service_tier` column (`default`, `flex`, `priority` or `batch`; Batch API usage is `batch`) and one row per day, project, model, tier and token unit type. Every usage row and token cost line item belongs to one of those tiers; `other` rows keep a null tier. Cost the export ties to a project stays `direct`. Cost without a project is spread only over usage of the same day, model, unit and tier, from projects with no direct cost there. Usage or cost with no counterpart in its own tier is its own `unmatched` row, never priced at another tier's rate, and the report must still tie out to the cost table. The same column and grain apply when only the cost or only the completion table is enabled.

The project in /app/integration_tests (profile `integration_tests` is set up for a local DuckDB file; run `dbt seed` before `dbt build`) must keep building on its own seeds, which have no tier columns, with every data test passing. The project stays SQL: the change goes in SQL models, macros and YAML, with no Python models. There's no network; dbt-core and dbt-duckdb are installed.
